summary.intent: Determine whether phase 71 (share-invite security and IPNS data-integrity API) of the CipherBox project needed further discussion, then run GSD phase planning to produce executable PLAN.md files for the phase.
summary.outcome: Confirmed phase 71 was already discussed on a branch, rebased it onto main, ran research/validation/pattern-mapping, and had the planner produce 7 plans across 3 waves — but the planner surfaced that locked decision D-01 (ownership check via `vaults`) was fundamentally broken since shares are always child items, not vault roots. This was resolved (switch to `ipns_records.user_id` check) and the user additionally decided on a full end-to-end column/property rename (`root_ipns_name`→`share_root_ipns_name`, purge "descriptor" naming entirely) plus folding D-04's CHECK constraint into the still-unreleased cutover migration; the planner was re-spawned to revise the plan set, work still in progress at transcript end.

repo: CipherBox shares are always child items (subfolders/files) inside a user's vault — the vault root itself is never shareable, so `shares.rootIpnsName`/`share_invites.rootIpnsName` never equals `vaults.root_ipns_name`; any ownership check based on the `vaults` table is a no-op or breaks all sharing.

`ipns_records.user_id` is documented as a non-authoritative 'denormalized creator marker' (authority is the record's Ed25519 signature), but it's the only server-side signal that exists for child-node ownership.

`readDescriptorRef`/`writeDescriptorRef` columns contain ONLY an ECIES-wrapped key (via wrapKey/unwrapKey) — no extra metadata despite entity comments claiming '+ metadata'; grant metadata (rootNodeId, rootGeneration, rootIpnsName) lives in separate columns.

`root_generation` is a pinned snapshot at grant-issuance time (anti-rollback baseline for phase 70.1's floor-store/high-water machinery), not derivable from live IPFS/IPNS record generation — must not be removed or replaced with a live lookup.
Write grant authority is presence-derived: writeDescriptorRef being non-NULL is itself the write grant (invariant T-66-E1); NULL = read-only.

The `shares`/`share_invites` tables are created via DROP+CREATE in the Phase 66 cutover migration, so schema is still greenfield/unreleased — renames can edit that migration in place rather than requiring a new forward ALTER TABLE migration.
`vaults.owner_id` has a unique index — exactly one vault row per user — so `vaults` can only ever authenticate vault-root ownership, never child/subfolder ownership.

Real access control for shares is cryptographic: a sharer can only produce a valid descriptor by calling `resolveShareWriteDescriptor` using keys they actually possess, so a bogus DB row alone can't grant real access — server-side ownership checks are defense-in-depth, not the primary boundary.
`getInvitesForItem` filters by `sharerId`, so a spoofed invite from an attacker pollutes only their own listing, not the victim's.

code.finding: rootIpnsName is set to params.item.ipnsName — the selected item's (always a child node's) IPNS name, never the vault root — which is why vaults-table-based ownership checks (D-01 as originally written) can't work.
Direct-share path also sets rootIpnsName = item.ipnsName (child node), confirming shares are always children-only, same as the invite flow.

Server enforces forward-only rootGeneration and seeds the recipient's durable generation floor from the grant's rootGeneration on first contact; regression throws ConflictException — this is the anti-rollback machinery hardened in phase 70.1.
Write descriptor construction is exactly bytesToHex(wrapKey(itemWriteKey, recipientPublicKey)) — no metadata packed in, confirming 'descriptor ref' naming is misleading vs actual column contents.

workflow: gsd-plan-phase's Nyquist Dimension 8 validation gate requires a `## Validation Architecture` section that only RESEARCH.md provides — skipping research can cause plan-checker failures on complex phases even when CONTEXT.md already has locked decisions.

A live planner subagent that halts on a genuine blocking finding can be resumed with the new decision rather than re-spawned cold, preserving its already-completed analysis of unaffected decisions (D-02...D-09 in this case).

Background subagents spawned during a GSD workflow (e.g. during research) can create and switch branches in the shared checkout out from under the orchestrator's own `git switch` — always re-verify HEAD/branch state before trusting it, especially after a long-running Agent task returns.
When measuring rename blast radius, use `git grep` for accurate counts — shell globs (e.g. via zsh) can mangle and undercount matches.

GSD plan-phase gate commits sometimes report `commit_failed` as a known false-negative; verify the commit actually landed via git log/show rather than retrying blindly (matches existing memory feedback-gsd-commit-reword-verify-first).

friction: Planner initially flagged 'wrong branch, not committed' warning that was actually incorrect — caused by a background subagent switching branches during research; required manual reconciliation via git log/branch inspection before proceeding.
zsh glob mangling gave inaccurate rename blast-radius counts on the first attempt, requiring a redo with git grep.

Locked decision D-01 from a prior discussion session turned out to rest on a false premise (that shares could point at vault roots), only caught by the planner grepping real call sites — meaning the earlier /gsd-discuss-phase output was itself subtly wrong despite being 'exhaustive'.
Entity code comments describing readDescriptorRef/writeDescriptorRef as containing '+ metadata' were inaccurate and had to be disproven by tracing actual construction/consumption code.
open_items: Planner re-spawned to revise the 7-plan set incorporating: D-01 amendment (ipns_records check), D-10 full end-to-end rename (purge 'descriptor' naming, root_ipns_name→shareRootIpnsName/share_root_ipns_name across TS/API/Rust, ~21 share/invite-domain files), and D-04 folded into the in-place cutover migration edit (no forward migration, no migration:run blocking gate) — not yet complete at end of transcript.
Duplicate/stale branch `feat/phase-71-share-invite-security` (stuck at the research commit) should be deleted once confirmed safe — deferred pending user OK.
Plan set has not yet been committed nor run through gsd-plan-checker — pending planner's revised output.

SC#3 in ROADMAP.md may still need trimming to drop the root-uniqueness index language (superseded by discussion finding that vaults.owner_id uniqueness already enforces it), deferred to GSD tooling per user instruction rather than manual edit.
